name: Anonymous Caribbean fleet-tracking company
description: The founder has run a fleet-tracking company for ~12 years, selling GPS tracking and AI dashcams to commercial fleets across the Caribbean, with a smaller operation in Colombia (founder-stated).

mentions.evidence: ~370 clients, roughly $1.6M ARR, "on track for about 30% growth in the Caribbean this year" (founder-stated) Revenue per client ≈ $4.3k/year (my arithmetic from the two stated numbers) Not verified; no company name or website given.

sources.label: Reddit r/Entrepreneur post by u/imjp (5 Oct 2026, ~20:09 Warsaw)

mentions.indieAngle: Two ways in. (1) Fleet telematics for an underserved region where you speak the language and know the buyers, e.g. Polish/Ukrainian transport SMEs with 5–50 trucks, bundling the tachograph/e-TOLL/SENT paperwork. (2) Build the dunning glue he lacks: wire-transfer reconciliation + auto-suspend + late-fee invoicing for B2B hardware-subscription companies in multi-country markets.

whyItPrints: Hardware + monthly SaaS sold to trucking, logistics and government fleets in small island markets that big US/EU players ignore. Billing runs across 20+ territories by wire transfer. The founder's own problem is the boring part: "almost half our clients, about 170 of 370, pay late", and "some of our gov clients are pretty much always 90+ days late". The fix he's planning is automatic account disconnects, annual billing for bad payers and late fees (founder-stated, in comments).
